GOOGL.rationale: GOOGL is a high-quality franchise with accelerating revenue (~6% QoQ), a fortress balance sheet ($386.9B equity, $98.5B cash as of Q3 2025), and a Cloud business that is inflecting sharply (Q1 2026 Cloud revenue $20B +63% YoY, backlog $462B). Berkshire Hathaway's aggressive accumulation to 54M shares and Dow Jones inclusion signal institutional conviction. However, the stock is priced at a stretched 34.8x P/E (76th percentile of its 12-month range) with operating margin compressing from 33.9% to 30.5% over three quarters, and the 2.9% earnings yield sits 167bp below the 4.57% 10-year Treasury. FCF margins are guided to compress from 18% to ~5% as capex surges to $180-190B. The Gemini 3.5 Pro delay and ongoing regulatory headwinds (EU €4.1B fine upheld, DOJ antitrust) add execution and structural risk. Q2 earnings on July 22 are a near-term catalyst—consensus expects $116.8B revenue (+21.1% YoY) and Cloud of ~$22.2B—but the clean operating EPS run-rate (stripping Q1's $37.7B Anthropic/SpaceX gains) is not compelling at this multiple. The franchise is excellent but the price already reflects near-perfection; the score reflects strong fundamentals offset by stretched valuation and margin headwinds.
